title: Gluing coherent colimits along a monomorphism of indexing simplicial sets
statement: An infinity category means a simplicial set with fillers for every inner horn, where an inner horn is the union of the faces of the standard simplex except one face other than the first or last. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the nerve of $\{0<\cdots<n\}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Colimits are understood in the coherent mapping-space sense: a cocone with vertex $L$ is a colimit when, for every object $T$, composition induces an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}(L,T)$ to the space of coherent cocones with vertex $T$. Let $A\to B$ and $A\to D$ be maps of simplicial sets, with $A\to D$ degreewise injective, and let $K=B\amalg_A D$ be their pushout in simplicial sets. Let $p:K\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in an infinity category. Suppose its restrictions to $B,A,D$ have colimits $X,Y,Z$, respectively, equipped with colimit cocones. Restriction of cocones induces a coherent span $X\leftarrow Y\to Z$, determined up to a contractible space of choices. If this span has a pushout $P$ in $\mathcal C$, then $p$ has a colimit, and $P$ with its induced cocone is such a colimit. No finiteness condition on $A,B,D$ and no existence of other colimits in $\mathcal C$ is assumed.
